title: Good Is the Heavenly King
description: Good Is the Heavenly King in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 859 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Blessings of Spring”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Good is the heav-enly King, Who makes the earth his care, Vis-its the pas-tures ev-ery spring, And bids the grass ap-pear.

lines: Who makes the earth his care,
Pour out their blessings from the sky,
The meadows, dressed in all their pride,
Thy ways abound with blessings still,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
